q: Can the paper's headline quantitative claim (per-drug AUC > 0.80 on 8 of 13 antibiotics) be reproduced by refitting the SVM-SGD ensemble on a modern re-derivation of the 1595-strain allele presence-absence matrix?
basis: The replication verified the paper's feature lists (MOESM4/5/9) and internal LOR/label consistency (809/809), but the raw per-strain x per-allele matrix is not distributed. The AUC > 0.80 headline was therefore not exercised. It is the single largest gap in this PARTIAL verdict.
next_steps: Crosswalk the 1595 PATRIC accessions to current BV-BRC IDs (post-2022 migration), rebuild the pan-genome via CD-HIT or PPanGGOLiN at the same identity threshold the paper used, generate the allele presence-absence matrix, and refit an SVM-SGD ensemble with 5-fold CV per drug. Report per-drug AUC/AUPRC vs the paper's Supp Fig 5. Free-tier compute: NCBI datasets + local CPU pan-genome build; no GPU needed.

q: Do modern deep-learning AMR predictors (e.g., protein-language-model embeddings of the same allele set, or graph-neural-network encodings of the epistatic interaction network) improve on the paper's SVM baseline for the harder drugs (ethionamide, 4-aminosalicylic acid) where MI failed to surface canonical targets in the top-40?
basis: The paper's own Table 1 shows SVM is required to recover ethA (ethionamide) and folC (4-aminosalicylic acid) because their AMR genetics are diffuse. Modern PLM embeddings (ESM-2, ProtT5) may capture functional signal that allele one-hot encodings miss.
next_steps: Encode each of the 254 AMR-panel alleles with ESM-2 (free HuggingFace weights); build a simple logistic-regression head per drug on strain-level embedding aggregates; compare per-drug AUC to Kavvas SVM baseline. Free compute: ESM-2 650M runs on a single M-series Mac or free Colab GPU.

q: Do the 24 newly-proposed AMR-candidate genes (Table 2) show independent functional or clinical validation in the M. tuberculosis literature published 2019-2026?
basis: The replication confirms 23/23 of the Table 2 genes appear in the ML-derived 254-panel, but does not check whether the field has since experimentally validated any of them. Rv3848, embR, oxcA, and mmpL11 are plausibly druggable but Rv3129, Rv3471c, Rv0044c, Rv0954 are hypothetical proteins as of 2018.
next_steps: PubMed/Semantic Scholar search 2019-2026 restricted to M. tuberculosis + each Rv-ID or gene name; classify hits as (a) experimental knockout MIC shift, (b) allele-level phenotype-genotype association in a new cohort, (c) computational-only re-analysis, or (d) not cited. Report validation rate. Free: S2 API key available, PubMed E-utils.

q: Does the paper's reference-agnostic allele pan-genome generalize across mycobacterial species (M. bovis, M. leprae, M. abscessus) or does it capture M. tuberculosis-specific resistance mechanisms only?
basis: Kavvas et al. restricted to M. tuberculosis. The MI/SVM/epistasis machinery is species-agnostic in principle, but AMR mechanisms in M. abscessus (efflux pump dominated) and M. leprae (unculturable, uses different targets) differ substantially. Cross-species performance is untested.
next_steps: Assemble a small BV-BRC pull of M. bovis + M. abscessus strains with AMR phenotypes (~200 strains each), build the allele pan-genome jointly with the M. tuberculosis set, and check whether the Kavvas Table 1 known-gene recovery holds when the model is trained pan-species vs Mtb-only. Free: BV-BRC API + local CPU pan-genome build.

q: Can phylogenetic priors (a strain-level MSA-derived tree used as a random-effect covariate) tighten the 232-vs-94 epistasis discrepancy and reduce false-positive gene-gene interactions caused by population structure?
basis: The replication found 232 BH-significant epistatic pairs vs the paper's 94, without applying the paper's per-class top-60 pre-filter. A well-known confounder in bacterial GWAS/epistasis is population structure (MDR lineages carry co-inherited mutation blocks that look epistatic but are just lineage markers). The paper does not explicitly correct for phylogeny.
next_steps: Build a maximum-likelihood tree of the 1595 strains from concatenated core-gene alignments (IQ-TREE, free); fit a mixed-effects logistic regression per candidate pair with strain lineage as a random effect (statsmodels or pyGWAS); compare the count of surviving pairs to the paper's 94 and our uncorrected 232. Free compute: laptop-scale.
